$comment: Lint baseline (PHASE-0 T3). Every count below may only FALL: check-lint-baseline.mjs fails the build when any rule or diagnostic code exceeds its pin, when an unpinned rule reports findings, or when either total rises. Counts are PER RULE, not just totals, so a rise in one rule cannot hide behind a fall in another. Seeded 2026-07-27 at commit fc662b6 from the commands recorded in each section, run on a clean, instrument-free tree. The eslint rules are all severity `warn` in eslint.config.js on purpose — the tree has hundreds of pre-existing findings and error-mode would be unshippable; this file is the enforcement, not the severity. To LOWER entries after real fixes: node deploy/checks/check-lint-baseline.mjs --tighten. To RAISE one, or to admit a newly enabled rule, edit this file BY HAND in a gate-side-only commit — that edit is meant to be seen and reviewed. No tool raises a number.

eslint.$comment: Findings by rule id. `--no-inline-config` is part of the command and is not optional: without it a one-line eslint-disable comment lowers the count without fixing anything. no-constant-binary-expression is pinned at 0 — the rule IS enabled and the tree is genuinely clean of it, so any future finding is a rise from zero.
eslint.$raise-no-restricted-imports: 89 -> 90, PHASE-3 T5 opening rider (2026-08-01), by hand. ONE new `node:fs` site: packages/server/src/memory/assembly-validation-sink.ts, the durable divergence sink T4's detect-only window needs — its evidence had been going to dojo.log, which logger.ts rotates at 10MB keeping one backup, measured at ababf11 as 16m14s of total retained history for a SEVEN-DAY window, with T4's own 17 day-0 lines already unrecoverable. The one alternative that would have kept this count flat was routing the append through logger.ts, which already imports fs — and it was REFUSED on measurement, not taste: logger.ts resolves LOG_DIR from os.homedir() at MODULE LOAD, so a sink built on it could not be tested against a redirected HOME without making a foundational module's path resolution lazy, i.e. changing the logging hot path to hold a lint count flat. This rule is advisory by its own message and exists to measure the surface Phase 5's brokers must route; this entry is that surface growing by one, named, with its file, so Phase 5 inherits a count it can trust rather than one that was gamed.
eslint.$raise-no-restricted-imports-t7: 90 -> 91, PHASE-3 T7 Step 2 (2026-08-01), by hand. ONE new `node:fs` site: packages/server/src/agent/v2/re-answer-sink.ts, the durable sink the 7-day RE-ANSWER QUIET WINDOW needs. Same measurement as T5's entry above, RE-DERIVED at T7's own HEAD rather than inherited: dojo.log.1 (19,522,717 bytes) spans 06:51:12.869Z -> 06:52:14.145Z and dojo.log (6,635,551 bytes) spans 06:52:14.124Z -> 06:55:27.542Z, i.e. 4 MINUTES 15 SECONDS of total retained history for a SEVEN-DAY window. The same alternative was available and refused for the same measured reason (logger.ts resolves LOG_DIR from os.homedir() at MODULE LOAD, so a sink built on it cannot be tested against a redirected HOME without making the logging hot path lazy to hold a lint count flat). THE SURFACE IS TEMPORARY BY DESIGN AND ITS RETIREMENT IS DATED: PHASE-3.md T7 Step 2 deletes the detector after the quiet window and this sink goes with it, and T9's exit gate greps for the detector. Phase 5 inherits a count that is due to fall by one, not a permanent addition.

unusedSymbols.$comment: Findings by TypeScript diagnostic code, from tsconfig.lint.json (noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters). That config is consumed ONLY by `npm run lint:types` — never by the build and never by `npm run typecheck` — so the unused-symbol population is counted without breaking either. TS6133 = declared but never read; TS6192 = all imports in a declaration unused; TS6196 = declared but never used (type position). 116 of the 118 sit in packages/server; the other 2 are in packages/shared, which the server program pulls in through its project reference.
